title: MiniMax H3 character swap
description: Changes the person in your clip into the character in your picture, with MiniMax H3 on Comfy Cloud. Give a clip, a character picture and what to change. H3 reads the clip as a reference video, so the new person copies its movement. One pass covers 5 to 15 seconds. Comfy Cloud bills H3 by the machine time it uses.

evidence: 2026-10-27: graph cut from Comfy's own video_minimax_h3_r2v template, the ref2va pass: the clip goes in as reference video frames (GetVideoComponents), the picture as the first reference image, and the prompt names both with <Video 1> and <Picture 1>. The sampler is res_multistep with the simple scheduler, 20 steps, 24 fps, and the video and audio VAE decode the one packed latent into a clip with sound. length is the frame count at 24 fps (124 is about 5 s); Comfy's template steps it by 17 to the trained range of about 124 to 362 frames (5 to 15 s).

Not yet run on Comfy Cloud: this task spent no credits, so no real swap exists yet. The model file names come from Comfy's template notes of 2026-10-27 and are the four files any H3 ref2va run needs; the turbo LoRA the template offers (minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1) is left out because no cloud model list can be read from here, and the graph runs without it at 20 steps.

One pass only: the 124-frame relay windows with history that Openjutsu-style runs use for clips longer than 15 s are not part of this pack yet; a longer clip needs the same chunking SCAIL-2 already has.

2026-10-27: the model file names were checked against Comfy Cloud's own node list (GET /api/object_info). The diffusion model, the text encoder and the audio VAE were there as written; the video VAE was not — Cloud carries minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors, so the graph names that one. Cloud has every node this graph uses, and its CLIPLoader offers the minimax type.
